mainTopic: The husband's physical fitness for the סוטה process; the new פרק כשם שהמים: the water checks the בועל, she is forbidden to him, and the teachings said 'on that day'.
overview: The amud first finishes a comparison between husband and wife. A husband who is lame, has no hands, or cannot speak cannot make his wife drink, just as such a wife cannot drink. Then פרק ארוסה closes and a new פרק opens. Its משנה teaches that the water checks the בועל just as it checks the woman. It also teaches that she is forbidden to the בועל just as she is forbidden to her husband. רבי עקיבא and רבי learn this second rule from the word נטמאה in different ways. The משנה then lists more teachings said 'on that day': a שני loaf makes a שלישי impure, the 1000 and 2000 אמות around the cities of the לויים, how בני ישראל sang שירת הים, and that איוב served ה׳ out of love. After two of these teachings (the שלישי loaf and איוב), רבי יהושע wishes his teacher רבן יוחנן בן זכאי could see it. Finally the גמרא begins by asking who 'him' in the משנה means, and this question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A lame or handless husband cannot make his wife drink
steps.stepSummary: The wife must be able to stand and to hold the מנחה. So the husband must also be able to stand and have hands, or he cannot make her drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the כהן stands the woman before ה׳ and places the offering in her hands. So she must be able to stand and must have hands. In the same way, if the husband was lame or had no hands, he could not make her drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that compares the husband to the wife. Whatever physical ability disqualifies her also disqualifies him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires the woman to be 'stood up' and to have the offering placed 'in her hands.' So a lame woman or one without hands cannot drink. The teaching then mirrors this onto the husband: if he is lame or handless, the process cannot happen either.

keyTerms.meaning: Lame; someone who cannot walk or stand properly
Makes her drink (the husband causing his wife to drink the סוטה water)
So too him; the same rule applies to the husband

phrases.english: "And the priest shall stand the woman before the Lord
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:18

phrases.english: ...and place in her hands"
phrases.notes: The dots skip part of the פסוק. The point is that she has to stand and has to have hands.

phrases.english: — so too him —
if he was lame or without hands,
he would not make her drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ הוּא — אִם הָיָה חִיגֵּר אוֹ גִידֵּם, לֹא הָיָה מַשְׁקָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a comparison that began before this section: the husband is treated like the wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who is lame or handless cannot make his wife drink, just as such a wife cannot drink.

steps.title: A mute husband cannot make his wife drink
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי adds a third case. A mute wife cannot drink because she must say 'אמן אמן'. So a mute husband cannot make her drink either.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: a mute woman did not drink, because the פסוק says she must say 'אמן, אמן'. In the same way, if the husband was mute, he could not make her drink.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי adds another example to the same husband-wife comparison. This time the issue is being able to speak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman has to answer 'אמן אמן' out loud, so a mute woman is excluded. מר בר רב אשי applies the same pattern to the husband: if he cannot speak, he cannot make her drink.

keyTerms.meaning: A mute woman / a mute man; someone who cannot speak
As it is written; introduces a פסוק as the source
The woman's spoken acceptance of the oath

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi says:
Just as a mute woman would not drink,
as it is written: "And the woman shall say: Amen, Amen,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:22

phrases.english: so too him — if he was mute,
he would not make her drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִילֶּמֶת לֹא הָיְתָה שׁוֹתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case (being mute) using the same husband-like-wife pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mute husband cannot make his wife drink, just as a mute wife cannot drink.
steps.whatToRemember: Whatever physical ability the סוטה process needs from the wife (standing, hands, speech), the husband needs too.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק ארוסה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line marks the end of the פרק called ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק ארוסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק named ארוסה ends here with the standard closing formula. A new פרק is about to begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a legal statement. It is the customary farewell said when finishing a פרק. It signals that the topic is about to shift to a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said when finishing a פרק
A betrothed woman; also the name of the פרק that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you, Arusa

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק that the previous steps finished.

steps.title: The water checks the בועל too
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה. The water tests the בועל just as it tests the woman, learned from the word 'ובאו' written twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the water checks her, so too the water checks him (the בועל). The פסוק says 'and it shall enter' twice.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It teaches that the bitter water affects not only the woman but also the man she was suspected with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ובאו' ('and it shall enter') appears twice in the סוטה section. The משנה reads the repetition as hinting at two people being checked: the woman and the בועל. So if she is guilty, he is struck as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Check, test; the water tests whether she sinned
And it shall enter; the word written twice in the פסוקים
As it is said; introduces the פסוק that is the source

phrases.english: Just as the water checks her,
so too the water checks him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' here is the man she was suspected with, not her husband.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And it shall enter," "And it shall enter."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:24 and 5:27

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתָהּ, כָּךְ הַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק and a new topic after the closing formula.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה water tests the בועל as well as the woman.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Him' (אותו) in this משנה means the בועל, not the husband. The husband was the topic just before, so it is easy to mix them up.

steps.title: She is forbidden to the בועל as well as to her husband
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא teaches that the woman is forbidden to the בועל just as she is forbidden to her husband. He learns this from the word 'נטמאה' and the second form 'ונטמאה' with an extra ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as she is forbidden to her husband, so she is forbidden to the בועל. The פסוק says 'is defiled' and also 'and is defiled.' These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second parallel. The woman becomes forbidden to the man she was suspected with, not only to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says 'נטמאה' and a later one says 'ונטמאה' with an extra letter ו. רבי עקיבא reads that extra ו as adding a second prohibition: forbidden to the husband, and also to the בועל. The phrase 'דברי רבי עקיבא' tells us this is his view, which sets up other opinions that come next.

keyTerms.meaning: The man she was suspected of being with
She is defiled / and she is defiled; the extra ו teaches an added prohibition

phrases.english: Just as she is forbidden to the husband —
so she is forbidden to the paramour,
as it is stated: "Is defiled," "And is defiled,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14 and 5:29. The second one has an extra ו, and רבי עקיבא learns from that extra letter.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֲסוּרָה לַבַּעַל — כָּךְ אֲסוּרָה לַבּוֹעֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second 'just as... so too' parallel in the same משנה, now about who she is forbidden to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, a סוטה is forbidden to the בועל just as she is forbidden to her husband, learned from the extra ו in 'ונטמאה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule: even if she is later divorced, she may not marry the man she was suspected with.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives two parallels. The water checks the בועל like it checks her. She is forbidden to the בועל like she is forbidden to the husband. רבי עקיבא learns the second one from the extra ו.

steps.title: זכריה בן הקצב taught the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע reports that זכריה בן הקצב used to teach the same idea as רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: This is how זכריה בן הקצב used to explain it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע tells us that רבי עקיבא's teaching from the last step was also taught earlier by זכריה בן הקצב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. רבי יהושע gives the same idea an older source: the woman is forbidden to the בועל just as she is forbidden to her husband. This shows the idea did not start with רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: This is how he used to explain the פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב,
phrases.english: This is how Zecharia ben HaKatzav used to expound.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an earlier source for the teaching in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זכריה בן הקצב taught the same thing as רבי עקיבא: the woman is forbidden to both the husband and the בועל.

steps.title: רבי learns it from the word being written twice
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the word 'נטמאה' appears twice in the section. One time is for the husband and one time is for the בועל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: The two times the פרשה says 'she was defiled' are one for the husband and one for the בועל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his own way to reach the same law. He does not use the extra letter ו. He uses the fact that the word is written two times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learned the law from the extra ו in 'ונטמאה.' רבי counts the two places where the word appears. He gives one to the husband and one to the בועל. The result is the same, but the source is different.

keyTerms.meaning: The section of the תורה, here the section about the סוטה

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
The two times that are stated in the passage
"she was defiled," "and she was defiled"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:14 and במדבר 5:29.

phrases.english: one for the husband and one for the adulterer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים הָאֲמוּרִים בַּפָּרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same law as step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'נטמאה' is written twice: once to forbid her to the husband and once to forbid her to the בועל.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that the סוטה is forbidden to both the husband and the בועל. They only disagree about where the פסוק shows it: the extra ו (רבי עקיבא) or the word written twice (רבי).

steps.title: A second-level loaf makes a third loaf impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads 'יטמא' as 'it will make others impure.' So a second-level loaf can make another food impure at the third level.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day רבי עקיבא explained: 'Every earthenware vessel that one of them falls into, everything inside it shall become impure.' The פסוק does not say 'is impure.' It says 'shall become impure,' which means it can make others impure. This teaches that a second-level loaf makes a third one impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings another teaching that רבי עקיבא taught on that same day. This one is about טומאה, not about the סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food inside the vessel is at the second level of טומאה. רבי עקיבא reads 'יטמא' as pointing forward: this food can go on and make other food impure. So a שני can create a שלישי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall become impure.' רבי עקיבא reads it as able to make others impure
A loaf at the second level of impurity

phrases.english: On that day Rabbi Akiva expounded:
phrases.notes: 'That day' is the day רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was made the head.

phrases.aramaic: ״וּכְלִי חֶרֶשׂ אֲשֶׁר יִפֹּל מֵהֶם אֶל תּוֹכוֹ
phrases.english: "And every earthenware vessel into which any of them falls,"
"whatever is inside it shall become impure"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:33.

phrases.english: It does not say "is impure" but rather "shall become impure,"
to make others impure.
This teaches about a second-level loaf
that it makes the third impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new, unrelated teaching from the same day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loaf at the second level of טומאה makes other food impure at the third level. This is learned from 'יטמא.'
steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. It is in the משנה only because רבי עקיבא taught it on the same day, not because it is connected to the סוטה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע wishes his teacher could see this
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע remembers that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was worried that a later generation would treat a third-level loaf as pure, since there was no פסוק for it. Now רבי עקיבא has found the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: Who will remove the dust from your eyes, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי? You used to say that a later generation would declare a third-level loaf pure, because no פסוק in the תורה says it is impure. But look, רבי עקיבא your student brings a פסוק from the תורה that it is impure: 'Whatever is in it shall become impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע reacts to step 8. He praises רבי עקיבא's teaching and speaks to his late teacher רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי feared that without a פסוק, people would one day call a ככר שלישי pure. רבי עקיבא's reading of 'יטמא' gives exactly that missing source. So the worry is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who will remove the dust from your eyes.' A wish that the dead person could come back and see

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
Who will uncover the dust from your eyes,
phrases.notes: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי had already died. רבי יהושע wishes he were alive to see this.

phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
for you used to say:
In the future, another generation is going
to declare a third-level loaf pure,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא,
phrases.english: since there is no verse in the Torah that it is impure.
But look, Rabbi Akiva your student

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא לוֹ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא,
phrases.english: brings a verse from the Torah that it is impure,
as it says: "Whatever is inside it shall become impure."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי יְגַלֶּה עָפָר מֵעֵינֶיךָ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 8 and shows how much that teaching matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's teaching gives a תורה source for the טומאה of a ככר שלישי. This answers רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's worry.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a teaching from a פסוק protects a law from being forgotten or dropped by later generations.

steps.title: Two verses about the land around the Levite cities
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא quotes two פסוקים about the open land around the cities of the לויים. One says two thousand אמות and the other says one thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day רבי עקיבא explained: 'You shall measure outside the city, on the east side, two thousand אמות.' But another פסוק says: 'From the wall of the city and outward, one thousand אמות all around.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a third teaching from that day. This line only sets up the problem: two פסוקים give different numbers. The answer comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק measures two thousand אמות outside the city. The other measures one thousand אמות from the wall. They seem to contradict each other. This prepares for רבי עקיבא's answer, which will explain what each number is for.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And another פסוק says.' Used to set two פסוקים against each other

phrases.english: On that day Rabbi Akiva expounded:
"And you shall measure outside the city

phrases.aramaic: אֶת פְּאַת קֵדְמָה אַלְפַּיִם בָּאַמָּה וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: the east side, two thousand cubits, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:5. This is about the cities given to the לויים.

phrases.english: And another verse says:
"From the wall of the city and outward
one thousand cubits all around."
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, unrelated teaching from the same day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two פסוקים about the land around the cities of the לויים give different measurements (2000 vs. 1000 אמות). This sets up the explanation that follows.

steps.title: One thousand is the מגרש, two thousand is the תחום שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא settles the clash between the two numbers. One thousand אמות are the מגרש, and two thousand אמות are the תחום שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We cannot say the area is only one thousand אמות, because the פסוק also says two thousand. And we cannot say it is two thousand, because the פסוק also says one thousand. So how do they fit? One thousand אמות is the open land, and two thousand אמות is the תחום שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the contradiction he set up in the last step. Each number is talking about a different thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First he shows that neither number can simply cancel the other, because both are written in the תורה. Then he gives each number its own job. The thousand is the מגרש, and the two thousand is the distance a person may walk on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: So how does it work? (used to bring two facts together)
Open land around the cities of the לויים
The Shabbos boundary, how far a person may walk on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי עקיבא finds a פסוק behind the two-thousand-אמה distance of תחום שבת.

phrases.english: It is impossible to say one thousand cubits,
since two thousand cubits was already stated.
And it is impossible to say two thousand cubits,
since one thousand cubits was already stated.
So how does it work?
One thousand cubits is the open land,
and two thousand cubits is the Shabbos boundary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between the two פסוקים quoted in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two numbers into two different areas
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to give two different sizes for the same area.
steps.terutzMaskana: One thousand אמות is the מגרש, and two thousand אמות is the תחום שבת.

steps.title: Another reading: one thousand of open land, two thousand of fields and vineyards
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees the thousand is the מגרש. He says the two thousand are fields and vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר, the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, says: one thousand אמות are open land, and two thousand אמות are fields and vineyards.
steps.whatsHappening: A different תנא gives another way to fit the two numbers together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that the thousand אמות are the מגרש. But he says the two thousand are more land given to the לויים for planting, not the תחום שבת. So by his reading, these פסוקים say nothing about the תחום שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים say the thousand אמות are the מגרש. They argue only about the two thousand: רבי עקיבא says תחום שבת, and רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי says fields and vineyards.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says:
One thousand cubits is open land,
and two thousand cubits is fields and vineyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way to fit the two numbers than רבי עקיבא's in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One thousand אמות are the מגרש, and two thousand אמות are fields and vineyards.

steps.title: The extra word 'saying' shows the people answered after משה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from the extra word 'לאמר' in אז ישיר. בני ישראל repeated a line after each line משה sang, like answering in הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day רבי עקיבא explained the פסוק 'Then משה and בני ישראל sang this song to ה׳, and said, saying.' The פסוק did not need the word 'saying,' so why is it there? It teaches that בני ישראל answered in song after משה on each and every line, the way people answer in הלל: 'I will sing to ה׳, for He is highly exalted.' That is why it says 'saying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new teaching that רבי עקיבא gave on the same day. It is about how בני ישראל sang שירת הים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ויאמרו' already tells us they spoke, so 'לאמר' looks extra. רבי עקיבא says the extra word teaches the way they sang. משה said each line, and the people answered with a set line, like a crowd answering in הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: There was no need for the פסוק to say this (so it must teach something)
The praise said on holidays, where the crowd answers the leader

phrases.english: On that day Rabbi Akiva expounded:
"Then Moshe and the children of Israel sang
this song to ה׳
and they said, saying,"
phrases.notes: שמות 15:1

phrases.english: for there was no need for the verse to say "saying,"
so why does the verse say "saying"?
It teaches that Israel would answer in song
after Moshe
on each and every statement,
like those who recite Hallel:
phrases.notes: The ה in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: ("I will sing to ה׳, for He is highly exalted.")
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets.

phrases.english: That is why "saying" is stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching from the same day, not connected to the מגרש topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra word 'לאמר' teaches that בני ישראל repeated a refrain after each line משה sang, like answering in הלל.

steps.title: They sang it like שמע, not like הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה disagrees with רבי עקיבא. He says the people sang together with משה, the way שמע is said, not by answering a refrain like in הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: they sang the way people say שמע, not the way people say הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה gives a different picture of how בני ישראל sang the שירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said the people answered with one refrain after each line. רבי נחמיה says they said the words of the song themselves along with משה. So the people sang the actual words, not just a repeated line.

keyTerms.meaning: קריאת שמע, which the crowd says together

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים agree that the people sang after משה. They argue only about how. רבי עקיבא says the people answered with one repeated line. רבי נחמיה says they sang the words themselves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
like those who recite Shema,
phrases.notes: He means the people said the words together with משה, like a group saying שמע.

phrases.english: and not like those who recite Hallel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא's picture in step 13 of how the people sang.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בני ישראל sang the שירה the way שמע is said, not the way הלל is answered.

steps.title: איוב served out of love
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן הורקנוס teaches that איוב served ה׳ only out of love, based on the פסוק הן יקטלני לו איחל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that same day, רבי יהושע בן הורקנוס taught: איוב served ה׳ only out of love. The פסוק says: 'Even if He kills me, I will still hope in Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching from that same day: רבי יהושע בן הורקנוס says איוב's service of ה׳ came from love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that איוב says he will keep hoping in ה׳ even if ה׳ kills him. A person serving only out of fear would not cling to ה׳ that way. Only love keeps someone loyal through such suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: On that very day: a set of teachings all said on one special day

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן הוּרְקָנוֹס:
phrases.english: On that day Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hurkenos expounded:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עָבַד אִיּוֹב אֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Job did not serve the Holy One, Blessed be He,
except out of love,
as it is stated: "Though He slay me, I will hope in Him."
phrases.notes: איוב 13:15

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן הוּרְקָנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from the same day as the earlier דרשות of רבי עקיבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב served ה׳ out of love

steps.title: The verse can be read two ways
steps.stepSummary: The proof is not yet clear. The word לו might mean 'I hope in Him' or 'I do not hope.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But the question is still open. Does the פסוק mean 'I hope in Him' or 'I do not hope'?
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching itself points out a weak spot in its own proof. This sets up the next step, which brings a stronger פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word means 'not', then איוב is saying 'If He kills me, I have no more hope.' That would show the opposite of love. So the first פסוק cannot settle the question alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter is still evenly balanced, so we cannot decide yet

phrases.english: But the matter is still evenly balanced:
Does it mean "for Him I hope,"
or "I do not hope"?
phrases.notes: The word can be read as לו (to Him) or as לא (not), and the two give opposite meanings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the proof in step 15 is not conclusive
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from הן יקטלני לו איחל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The key word has two possible meanings, and one of them gives the opposite result

steps.title: A second verse settles it: love
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק עד אגוע לא אסיר תמתי ממני shows that איוב stayed loyal to the end, so he served out of love.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'Until I die, I will not give up my innocence.' This shows that he acted out of love.
steps.whatsHappening: A second פסוק is brought to settle the doubt from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no word that can be read two ways. איוב clearly says he will hold on to his loyalty until he dies. That kind of lasting devotion shows love, so the first פסוק should also be read as 'I hope in Him.'
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן הורקנוס proves from עד אגוע לא אסיר תמתי ממני that איוב served ה׳ out of love.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states:
"Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me,"
phrases.notes: איוב 27:5

phrases.english: this teaches that he acted out of love.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the doubt raised in step 16
steps.raayaObject: That איוב served out of love
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 27:5, עד אגוע לא אסיר תמתי ממני

steps.title: רבי יהושע's cry to his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע wishes his late teacher רבן יוחנן בן זכאי could see this. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי taught that איוב served only out of fear, but a student's student has shown it was love.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: If only someone could brush the dust from your eyes, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי! All your life you taught that איוב served ה׳ only out of fear, because the פסוק says 'a man who was whole and straight, who feared God and stayed away from evil.' Now יהושע, your student's student, has taught that he served out of love.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע reacts with amazement to this new teaching. He wishes his teacher, who has passed away, could be alive to hear it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי relied on the words ירא אלהים, which show fear. The new דרשה shows a higher level, love. רבי יהושע is excited that a later student added something his own great teacher had not said.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will remove the dust from your eyes, meaning 'if only you were alive to see this'

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named יהושע here. The one speaking is רבי יהושע, the student of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. The יהושע he praises is רבי יהושע בן הורקנוס, who is his student's student.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views of איוב: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says he served out of fear, and רבי יהושע בן הורקנוס says out of love. Love is treated as the higher level.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
Who will remove the dirt from your eyes,
phrases.notes: His teacher had already died, so he means 'if only you could come back and see this.'

phrases.english: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai,
for you would teach all your days

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא עָבַד אִיּוֹב אֶת הַמָּקוֹם אֶלָּא מִיִּרְאָה,
phrases.english: that Job served the Omnipresent only out of fear,
as it is stated: "A man wholehearted and upright,
God-fearing, and shunning evil,"
phrases.notes: איוב 1:1

phrases.english: but now Yehoshua, the disciple of your disciple,
has taught that he acted out of love.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מִי יְגַלֶּה עָפָר מֵעֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A reaction to the conclusion of step 17, comparing it with the earlier view of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי held that איוב served out of fear, based on ירא אלהים. The new teaching shows he served out of love.

steps.title: Who is the man the water checks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking who אותו in the משנה refers to. It rejects the husband, since he did nothing wrong, and begins another suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins: Who does the משנה mean by 'him'? If you say it means the husband, what did the husband do wrong? And if you would say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה with a question about one word. It rejects the first possible answer and begins a new suggestion, which continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the water checks 'him' just as it checks her. The husband is ruled out because he committed no sin that the water would need to check. The words וכי תימא open the next try, which comes in the following lines.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins
And if you would say: the start of a new suggestion

phrases.english: GEMARA: "Him": to whom does it refer?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's line that just as the water checks her, it also checks him.

phrases.english: If we say to the husband,
what did the husband do?
And if you would say...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the 'him' whom the water checks along with the woman?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet given. The husband is rejected, and a new suggestion begins with וכי תימא.
